title: Share it with the world
content:
## What you'll get

Your app is live - now it's time to share the link, watch real people use it, and collect the feedback that'll help you make it even better.

---

## Share your public URL

Once your app is deployed, you have a **permanent public link** (something like `https://your-app-name.emergent.app`). Anyone can visit it - no login required unless you've built one into your app.

Copy the URL from your workspace and share it however you like:

- Text it to friends or family
- Post it in a group chat or on social media
- Email it to beta testers
- Add it to your portfolio

The link stays the same as long as your app is deployed, so you can share it once and people can keep visiting.

<Tip>
Your deployed app runs 24/7. Visitors don't need to wait for it to "wake up" - it's always ready.
</Tip>

---

## What your visitors see

When someone clicks your link, they see the exact version of your app that's currently deployed - the production environment. This is the polished, stable version you chose to make public (see [Preview vs Deployed](/preview-vs-deployed-separate) for the difference).

If you're still iterating in preview, those changes **won't** show up at the public URL until you redeploy. Your live app stays frozen at the last version you pushed, so it's safe to keep experimenting in the background.

## If something looks wrong

Check the **deployment status** in your workspace:

- **Green (Live)** - everything's running smoothly
- **Yellow (Degraded)** - the app is slow or partially working
- **Red (Down)** - something's broken

Click **Logs** in the deployment panel to see what's happening behind the scenes. You'll see every request, error message, and console output in real time - perfect for tracking down why a button isn't working or a page won't load.

<Tip title="Proactive debugging">
Check the Errors tab regularly, especially after pushing updates. Catching issues early helps maintain a smooth experience for your users.
</Tip>

If your app is crashing or running slowly, see [App slow, crashing or cold-starting](/app-slow-crashing-or-cold-starting) for troubleshooting steps.
